description:
A helper kernel may take a `bitstring` accumulator parameter and return it (alone or in a tuple); since kernel calls are inlined it stays the same append-only local. Still append-only; entry kernels still can't take bitstring inputs. Lifts the 'passing to another kernel' restriction from 'Can a kernel produce variable-length bit output, and in what form?' (defk-dtw.14) because Gorilla's multi-clause dod_bits(acc, dod) needs it.

Each accepted convenience construct needs: an Elixir-mode meaning, agreement tests (Defk.Case, both modes), and a docs/language.md entry. Decided in 'Which convenience constructs do the six target workloads need?' (defk-dtw.18); sketches on branch prototype/defk-dtw.18-sketches (prototypes/convenience_sketches.exs).

Done when the Gorilla dod_bits helper compiles and agrees, the accumulator survives a yield inside the inlined helper (forced-yield test), and passing an accumulator to an entry kernel is a compile error.

comments.text: Decisions: (1) A kernel with a bitstring parameter is a helper: only inlined, no NIF, no Elixir function, not in __defk_kernels__ (Elixir mode still defines its private function for callers). The compiler does not lower it standalone; its rejections surface where it is inlined (once, in the helper). (2) 'Entry kernel taking a bitstring' = a helper not reached from any non-helper kernel through the call graph; that is bitstring-use at the parameter, with a hint to call it from the kernel that builds the accumulator. No syntax for entry vs helper was added. (3) A variable passed at a helper's bitstring parameter position counts as an accumulator name (Defk.Bitstring.accumulator_names/2 + bits_params/1), so reduce: <<>> / acc = <<>> become the empty bitstring when the only append is in the helper. (4) Passing a bitstring to a non-bitstring parameter stays bitstring-use (message names the parameter and its type); passing a [u8] to a bitstring parameter is type-mismatch. (5) No runtime change: binding the parameter copies the defk_bits {nbits, slot}; defk_bits_end already copies when appending to an older value, so a helper appending to a value the caller still holds agrees (tested, also across forced yields in a helper loop). (6) dod_bits test kernel uses signed segments (defk-dki, merged from main) where the range fits, masking at the anchor's +64/+256/+2048 range ends and for the 32-bit case, which Elixir's signed segments truncate. Tests in test/bitstring_helper_test.exs.

title: Pass the bitstring accumulator through helper kernels
